PUSH REJECTED c46fe7cc, report /home/user/Nikaia/docs/briefs/yaml/y9-1027-group-label.md.report.md

The fix for #1027 is committed as c46fe7cc (`Fixes #1027`), but it is not on `develop`: the push was rejected because `develop` had moved on. Following the brief, I did not rebase, so the supervisor needs to rebase and push it.

- **Fix:** a group around a single element that is not a sequence or a choice is now written as that element, nested groups included. So `n:(P)`, `k:((P))` and `s:(text(digit+))` now bind their value. Labels also look through such groups for the `span(..)`, `text(..)` and literal cases, so `sp:(span(p))` and `t:(text(a:x b:y))` work too; I checked those two by hand.
- **Tests:** the new test failed on the unfixed compiler with the three "Cannot find value" errors (`n`, `k`, `s`) and passes now. `tests/compiler` at both settings passed (407), the guard set passed (24), clippy is clean, `packages/yaml` passed (10), and the pre-push check passed. The first `tests/compiler` run hit the 10-minute background limit, so I reran it with a longer limit.
- **Found:** an unrelated, older defect. A rule over `Bytes` that returns a captured literal, `x:"ab" eof -> { x }`, passes `nikaia check` but rustc refuses it with "Lifetime may not live long enough". This happens with or without a group, and it did before this change.
- **Changelog:** "A label on a group around one element (`n:(P)`, `k:((P))`, `s:(text(p))`) binds what the element yields, as Part II 10.8 says, instead of reaching rustc as an unknown name."
- **Disk:** the test cache is 5.8 GB, with 11 GB free on the disk and no new cache entry over 100 MB. I deleted my copy of the compiler binary from the scratchpad.
